what-is-a-guest-link.title: What an invitation link is
what-is-a-guest-link.summary: A link that belongs only to your household. You open it, see the invitation and reply — no account and no password.
what-is-a-guest-link.keywords: link invitation guest account password household what is it how it works qr
what-is-a-guest-link.where: The link you received from the host

body.p1: The host sent you a link by email, by message or printed as a QR code on the invitation. The link belongs to your household: whoever opens it can see the invitation and reply on your behalf. You do not need an account.
body.h1: What you find on the link

ul1.a: The invitation: what is being celebrated, when and where, with “See on the map”.
ul1.b: Your reply, which you can change until the deadline.
ul1.c: If the host has started them: the “When suits you?” poll, the “Who brings what” list, “Your seat” at the table, the programme and “Getting there”.
ul1.d: “Private request” — for a dietary or access need, read only by the organisers designated for it.

body.note1: If the host changes something (the date, the deadline, the questions), on your next visit you see the notice “Something changed since your last visit”.
body.note2: Keep the link to yourself and your family. If you lost it or it reached someone else, ask the host for a new one — the old one stops working.
body.p2: You change the page's language with the RO / EN switch.

answer-an-invitation.title: How to reply to an invitation
answer-an-invitation.summary: One question per screen: whether you are coming, how many of you and what else the host wants to know. At the end you check and send.
answer-an-invitation.keywords: reply answer rsvp coming cannot come maybe adults children change reply deadline confirm
answer-an-invitation.where: The link you received from the host

ol1.a: Open the link. At “Will you join us?” choose “Yes, gladly”, “Maybe — not sure yet” or “I can't make it”.
ol1.b: If you are coming, answer “How many adults are coming?” and “How many children are coming with you?” with the plus and minus buttons.
ol1.c: Answer the host's questions, if there are any: menu, allergies, accommodation, transport.
ol1.d: At “Where can we tell you if something changes?” you can leave an email address. It is not required.
ol1.e: At “Does everything look right?” look over your answers and press “Send reply”.

body.note1: About children we keep only their number. Please do not type a child's name, age or date of birth in any field.
body.p1: Open the link again and press “Change reply”. You can change it until the deadline shown. After the deadline you see “The reply deadline has passed”: write to the host directly.
body.p2: If the host cancels or postpones the event, the link tells you so. If you left an email address, you also receive a message.
body.p3: The message “Too many attempts” means the link was opened too many times in a short while. Try again a little later.

guest-privacy.title: What is known about you as a guest
guest-privacy.summary: We keep your household's reply and, about children, only their number. Other guests do not see your details.
guest-privacy.keywords: privacy guest personal data children email private who sees other guests suppliers
guest-privacy.where: The link you received from the host · the event's public page

ul1.a: What we keep: the household's reply (whether you are coming and how many), the answers to the host's questions and your email address, if you left one.
ul1.b: About children: only how many are coming. No names, no ages.
ul1.c: Who sees the reply: the host and their planning team. Contact details are seen only by the owner and the project manager.
ul1.d: Other guests do not see the guest list or your reply. At the tables, each person sees only their own seat.
ul1.e: Suppliers do not receive your name. They receive numbers: how many people, how many menus of one kind.

body.p1: What you write under “Private request” is read only by the organisers specifically designated for it — not other guests and not suppliers. The kitchen learns, for example, only “3 × gluten-free”.
body.p2: We use it only to tell you if something about the event changes. It is not required.
body.note1: On an event's public page you register without an account. If the places are taken, you can join the waiting list and you receive a single email if one frees up.
body.p3: For a request about your data, write to the host or see the “Privacy policy”, in the “Contact and reporting” section.
